properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued November 6 at 3:24PM MST until November 6 at 6:30PM MST by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Arroyo and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...East Central Cibola County in west central New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 630 PM MST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 323 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause arroyo and small stream flooding.
Between 0.3 and 0.7 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Acoma Pueblo.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Arroyos, streams, and normally dry rivers can become raging killer
currents in a matter of minutes. Water in arroyos can travel many
miles and take hours to reach your location from upstream rain areas.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT UNTIL 630 PM MST THIS EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Caribbean Waters of Puerto Rico from 10 NM to 17N, including the Coastal Waters of Saint Croix
properties.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued November 6 at 5:42PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
The areas affected include...
Caribbean waters of Puerto Rico from 10 NM to 17N, including the
coastal waters of Saint Croix...

* At 542 PM AST, Doppler radar indicated a group of strong
thunderstorms, capable of producing winds to around 30 knots and
possible waterspouts. These strong thunderstorms were located about
40 NM south of Guanica, moving northeast at 15 knots.

Locations impacted include...
Mainly open waters of Caribbean waters of Puerto Rico from 10 NM to
17N, including the coastal waters of Saint Croix.
properties.instruction:
Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or nearest law enforcement
agency. They will relay your report to the National Weather Service
office.

Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, lightning strikes, heavy downpours, and possible waterspouts.
Boaters should seek safe harbor immediately until this storm passes.

NWSheadline: STRONG THUNDERSTORMS OVER CARIBBEAN OFFSHORE WATERS
